root_causes.hypothesis: H1. No stop announcement to the ESP before the car stops, so the ESP never grants an unlimited standstill. hold_tsk_owned switches to HMS=4 on the first stopping frame below 1.0 m/s. On hill stops the planner lags, so OP's stopping state starts at or after the moment the wheels hit 0 (uphill), or below 1.0 m/s (slow downhill). On those stops ACC_07 never carries Anhalten / HMS=1 / Anhalteweg 0.3, and ESP_21 bit 63 (the ESP's ACC stopping procedure) never runs while the car is moving. Without that procedure the ESP treats the TSK's standstill braking as a time-limited standstill phase. TSK_Status goes to 6 a few seconds into the stop.
root_causes.evidence_for: (1) The replay study shows that the only CAN difference between hold_tsk_owned and its parent is the parent's 0.40 s stop-announcement window. The ACC block md5 is the same on all refs, and frame diffs are limited to [-2.36..-1.98] on flat and [+0.06..+0.44] on +11%. After that window, both send the same frames. (2) Every hold logged without a fault had that window while the car was still moving. Route 333 stop #2: HMS 1 at -2.37 s (v 1.01), bit 63 on at -2.34, HMS 4 at -1.97 (v 0.67), bit 63 off at -1.94; it then held 26.3 s at TSK 3 (stop #1 held 21.1 s). Route 332 at +2.4%: latch 2.10 s before standstill, held about 11 s. (3) Replay: on uphill stops with plan lag (0.04 s and 0.50 s), hold_tsk_owned sends HMS1 for 0.00 s and ACC_07 Anhalten never appears, HMS sequence 0>4>0. Onset-speed sweep: hold_tsk_owned's announcement is 0 frames whenever the stopping state starts at or below 1.01 m/s, so 'any hill' is effectively 'stopping state below 1 m/s'. (4) Route 338: accFaulted at 0:23 with v=0, about 3-4 s after the stop (1.3 m/s at 0:18, 0.5 at 0:19). That fits a short factory standstill limit: the VW wiki says ACC-low cars make the driver take over 'after a very short delay', and a T6.1 owner reports about 3 s. (5) RJ, PR #2764: 'MQB cars without an EPB will fault if the ESP holds the brakes for too long at a standstill' and 'If we transition from stopping to starting before the car has reached a standstill, we can ask for brake indefinitely'. RJ's code sends ACC_07 STOP below 9.5 km/h until bit 63 appears, then latches START. (6) The DBC has ESP_08 bit 14 ESP_Stillstandsphase_erschoepft ('standstill phase exhausted'). (7) The history repeatedly says that holding HMS 4 without a hold request faults (f30a396 'permanent HMS=4 -> SRBM'; 6bacc4d 'HMS=4 accumulates SRBM ... trips TSK'), and the user calls this 'an issue we have had previously'.
root_causes.evidence_against: No CAN trace of the 337/338 faults exists yet, so bit 63, HMS order, Brm and the time from standstill to fault are all unconfirmed. Route 337's stop time is unknown: the last speed event is at 3:13 and the fault at 3:35, so the 'few seconds' figure rests on route 338 alone. On flat stops hold_tsk_owned sends 0-1 HMS1 frames. If one frame does not start bit 63, H1 predicts that long flat stops fault too, and the user reported only hill faults (they may not have noticed, or the flat stops were short). That a short bit-63 episode grants an unlimited standstill comes from RJ and has not been shown on this car. Bit 53 was never seen, so what the ESP does internally is inferred.

root_causes.hypothesis: H3. The ESP rejects a start request that runs uninterrupted from about 0.5 m/s through the whole standstill (ACC_07 Anfahren / HMS 4 with negative accel) when no ACC_07 stop request came before it. It faults after a timeout. This is a variant of H1 in which the trigger is a plausibility/consistency check rather than a standstill timer. The cure is the same: an ACC_07 stop request while the car is still moving.
root_causes.likelihood: Medium (about 15%), shares the fix with H1
root_causes.evidence_for: Replay Q4: this is the only CAN pattern unique to hold_tsk_owned. On uphill stops with plan lag the ESP sees an unbroken start request from 0.49 m/s and ACC_07 never carries a stop request, while the parent always does. MEB note: 'ANFAHREN faults TSK if the hold manager isn't holding'. ESP_33 bit 38 (ESC_Konsistenz_ACC) and bit 45 exist as consistency flags.
root_causes.evidence_against: The parent sends the same steady 'start' combination (A6 Anhalten + A7 Anfahren/HMS4, accel -1.23) for 20-26 s without a fault, once one announcement has happened, so the combination is tolerated in itself. No consistency bit has been seen rising in any trace (route 332 fault F#1 b29=0; bits 38 and 45 were never reported set).

root_causes.hypothesis: H2. A hill-hold failure that does not depend on the announcement: at accel -1.2 the TSK's standstill torque on a grade is too low (if it subtracts grade), or the ESP flags slip at standstill (ESP_08 Abrutschen_Stillstand), and the TSK faults.
root_causes.evidence_for: The user ties the faults to hills. No log shows the parent holding a grade of 5% or more for longer than 3 s (+11.2% stop: driver braked at +0.34; -4.8%: 2.9 s). Brm at +2.4% was 97 raw against 141 on flat, so the torque level depends on grade or time in some way that is not understood.
root_causes.evidence_against: After the 0.4 s window, hold_tsk_owned's frames match the parent's exactly (replay), so H2 alone cannot explain why only hold_tsk_owned faults. It could only do so if every parent hill hold was short, and the route 339 stop table can show whether they were. Both faults were logged at v=0, and the user reported soft faults, not rollback. Route 339 (t2_accel_cap_launch: the parent's hold code on the same e558ce7 base) had no faults over 7 segments and 8 launches (hill stops unknown).

root_causes.hypothesis: H4. HMS 1<->4 cycling while OP is stopping and vEgo crosses 1.0 m/s slowly. Only hold_tsk_owned does this; it unlatches at v>=1.0 and relatches below. Under this hypothesis the cycling builds an ESP re-request count or sets bit 29, and the fault shows later at standstill.
root_causes.evidence_for: Replay of the -6% downhill stop at 1.10 m/s: hold_tsk_owned HMS sequence 0>1>4>1>4>1>4>1>4>0 (8 changes in 0.4 s at v 0.99-1.02); the parent stays at 0>1>4>0. Commits 6bacc4d and d861e6b blame 4->1 re-requests and cycling for TSK faults.
root_causes.evidence_against: On route 338 the car slowed at about 0.8 m/s2 near the stop (1.3 to 0.5 m/s in 1 s). The sweep shows 0 round trips at 0.5 m/s2 or more. The fault came 3-4 s after standstill, not during the approach. Uphill plan-lag stops never cross 1.0 in the stopping state.

root_causes.hypothesis: H5. Confounds: something else in the 337/338 drives. Candidates are e558ce7 planner behaviour (stop<->pid flips at standstill), driver pedal toggling (#2874), or the startup relay handover / a second ACC sender (route 338's fault is only 23 s into the drive; route 333 had 543 foreign ACC frames in its first 11 s; route 332 had a TSK 2->6 at 0:02 with no OP cause).
root_causes.evidence_for: Route 338's fault was at 0:23, early in the drive. The startup TSK fault on route 332 is still unexplained. Both T0 drives include e558ce7.
root_causes.evidence_against: Route 339 runs e558ce7 with the parent's hold code and had no faults. Route 337's fault was at 3:35, well after startup. Stop<->pid flips produce the same ACC_06 S<->G toggles on the parent (replay chatter scenario), so they do not explain why only T0 faults.

recommendation:
Build A first ('Early stop announcement triggered by speed, then HMS 4 held'). It should go on a new branch, e.g. hold_announce_early, off t2_lead2_phantom_fix (the same parent as hold_tsk_owned), and it changes only MQBStandstillManager in carcontroller.py. Gate it on the trace below, which takes the user a few minutes with the car off and no drive. Build or drive A only if the faulting stops on 337/338 show 'ESP ACC stopping procedure (bit 63): never on'.

Why A should not fault, point by point from evidence:
(1) The replay study shows that the only CAN difference between hold_tsk_owned (faulted in 2 of 2 drives on hills) and its parent (no faults on routes 332, 333 and 339) is a 0.40 s ACC_07 stop announcement: HMS 1, Anhalten and Anhalteweg 0.3. Every other frame is identical. So the fault follows that announcement being missing, not the TSK-owned hold itself.
(2) Every fault-free hold logged on this car had that announcement while the car was still moving, with ESP bit 63 on within 0.03 s and off within 0.03 s of HMS 4. Route 333 held 21.1 s and 26.3 s with the switch to HMS 4 1.97 s before standstill; route 332 held about 11 s at +2.4% with the switch 2.10 s before standstill.
(3) A sends exactly that 20-frame announcement on every stop, but triggers it by speed (vEgo < 1.5 m/s while braking), so the planner lag on hills cannot skip it. In the replay it finishes 1.34 s before wheels 0 on +11% with 0.04 s and 0.50 s plan lag, 2.34 s before on flat, and 5.96 s before on -6%, where hold_tsk_owned sends 0.00 s.
(4) After the window, A's frames are identical to the parent's held state: A6 Anhalten, A7 Anfahren/HMS 4, d 20.46, accel -1.23, the state that held 26 s.
(5) A never sends HMS 1 at standstill (0.00 s in all 9 replay scenarios) and does not change HMS at standstill except on a disengage or re-engage. That removes the r332 #5 zero-torque rollback mechanism, the parent's 4->1->4 dips (12 at standstill in the chatter case; 6bacc4d tied 4->1 to TSK=6), and hold_tsk_owned's 1<->4 cycling at 1.0 m/s.
(6) RJ, PR #2764 and his code: start an ESP stopping procedure, exit to start before standstill, then 'we can ask for brake indefinitely'.
A also needs no new CS field, no Params key and no acados change, and it does not touch the panda-checked accel.

What A does not cover (separate one-change branches later, only if a trace shows the need): TSK torque too low on +11% (H2: a stronger standstill accel); H8 frames, where ACC_06 Anfahren with negative accel might release the brake (move the starting threshold to 0.25 like upstream); re-engaging at standstill.

If the traces show bit 63 WAS on before standstill on a faulting stop, do not build A: H1 is refuted, so look at H2 (Brm and wheel pulses before the fault) or H4/H5 (fault classifier labels).
